thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — spun up Pelias-13B on staging today (fp16 baseline + int8/int6 quant experiments). Sharing rapid slice-level econ + quality notes.

ravi: thanks! what's the headline?

maya: short: int8 gives ~2x cost reduction vs fp16 with negligible GTN delta; int6 pushes to ~3.2x cost reduction but shows measurable regression on long summarization and entity recall. Latency changes small for median, but tails worsen on bursty traffic.

chris: can you drop the numbers so we can put into a short recommendation for product?

maya: paste of key numbers (small sample):
- slices: 4k multi-turn chats (avg 8 turns), 2.5k long-form summarization requests (>2k tokens), 3k single-turn completions
- fp16 P50/P95 (A100 test nodes): 48ms / 180ms
- int8 P50/P95: 52ms / 190ms
- int6 P50/P95: 58ms / 230ms
- p99: fp16 360ms, int8 400ms, int6 610ms (on burst sim)
- estimated token cost per 1M tokens: fp16 = $5.2k, int8 = $2.6k, int6 = $1.6k
- GTN eval (paired): int8 = -0.2% overall, int6 = -1.8% overall; for long summarization slice int6 = -3.9% ROUGE-L delta

ravi: where do quality fails concentrate?

maya: mostly two places: 1) long-context resolution (entity linking/recall drops on >2000 token context), 2) hallucination on multi-document synth tasks. Short Q&A and instruction following are largely intact.

chris: any mitigation ops changes we tried?

maya: a few operational knobs helped:
- enable aggressive prefix KV caching for repeated conversations (reduces effective compute for long chats)
- pin decode to int8 while keeping attention matmul paths int6 (hybrid-mode) — this recovered ~60% of the int6 quality gap in summaries while keeping cost ~2.7x vs fp16
- slightly lower max_batch_tokens for int6 (recommended 512 -> 384) to avoid packing variance causing p99 spikes

ravi: hybrid decode? explain briefly so product understands tradeoffs.

maya: hybrid = run forward attention/kv compute in int6 quant kernels but switch to int8 for the final softmax/prob computations and logits scaling. Practically we saw a small perf hit vs pure int6 but quality improved materially on named-entity recall. Worth a canary for non-critical long reads.

chris: how should GTN route? suggestions for product?

maya: proposal for GTN/product routing:
- Default chat routes: int8 (balanced econ + quality)
- Long-read/high-fidelity: fp16 or int8 fallback for contexts >1500 tokens
- Low-cost batch completions: int6 allowed behind an explicit feature flag and limited to <15% traffic initially
- Hybrid pilot: run hybrid decode on 10% of long-read traffic for 2 weeks to validate quality recovery

ravi: thresholds we can publish in the runbook?

maya: suggested scorecard thresholds:
- acceptance: GTN eval delta <= 0.5% for int8; <= 1.2% for int6 on short slices
- strict slices (summaries, multi-doc synth): require int6 delta <= 1.0% or opt out
- latency SLO: chat P95 <= 240ms; alert P99 > 550ms
- econ trigger: prefer quantization if per-token cost improvement >= 1.8x and quality within thresholds
- auto-rollback: trigger if GTN eval drops >1% relative in 30m window or product KPI drops by >2%

chris: A/B experiment design?

maya: simple AB: allocate 10% traffic to candidate quant (int6 or hybrid), hold 10% as control (fp16/int8 depending on lane) for 14 days. Track: GTN eval, completion accept rate, downstream conversion metric, and token spend delta. Ramp if no signal degradation.

ravi: ops impact for Dedicated clients?

maya: Dedicated: ship int8 as opt-in default; expose int6 toggle with per-model warnings in console; for reserved pools recommend a slow rollout and explicit SLA acknowledgement because p99 can vary. We'll include recommended tuning presets in the Dedicated docs.

ops-bot: Deploy note: pelias-13b-fp16 staging green. int8 canary -> 2026-04-02T15:22Z. int6/hybrid pilots scheduled.

chris: good work. Could you produce a short one-pager with the scorecard + a small example notebook (eval -> delta plots) and link it into the GTN runbook?

maya: yes prepping that now, will post in eng-ml drive and ping product. Link soon. :white_check_mark:

ravi: one more thought — try quant-aware prompt engineering (shorter context priming) as a non-invasive quality lift for int6. Might recover a few points without moving to fp16.

maya: noted, will add as an action item. Action list: maya -> upload scorecard + notebook; chris -> coordinate GTN experiment; ravi -> prepare Dedicated docs. Closing for now.
